_about: Part catalog. Unless a field is listed under `sources`, its value comes from the part's `source`. Compiled with help from Claude (AI).

parts.name: 1U structure
parts.blurb: A 10 cm cube. Cheap to launch, but there is very little room or power, and no place for a fast antenna.

parts.name: 3U structure
parts.blurb: Three cubes in a stack. The workhorse size for science CubeSats.

parts.name: 6U structure
parts.blurb: Two 3U stacks side by side. Room for a big instrument, at twice the launch price.

parts.name: Body panel, 1U
parts.blurb: Two solar cells fixed to one face. Makes power only when that face sees the Sun.

parts.name: Body panel, 3U
parts.blurb: Seven solar cells fixed to one face. Simple and light, but it cannot follow the Sun.

parts.name: Deployable wing
parts.blurb: Folds flat for launch, then swings out. With good attitude control it stays pointed at the Sun.

parts.name: Battery, 10 Wh
parts.blurb: Keeps the spacecraft alive in Earth's shadow. Small and light.

parts.name: Battery, 20 Wh
parts.blurb: Twice the stored energy for twice the mass.

parts.name: Battery, 40 Wh
parts.blurb: Plenty of energy for power-hungry payloads. Heavy.

parts.name: Flight computer
parts.blurb: A flight-proven low-power processor. Enough for simple instruments.

parts.name: Flight computer, high performance
parts.blurb: Three times the processing and memory, for cameras and on-board data handling. Draws more power.

parts.name: Attitude control, magnetic
parts.blurb: Pushes against Earth's magnetic field to stop tumbling. Coarse pointing only.

parts.name: Attitude control, reaction wheels
parts.blurb: Three spinning wheels turn the spacecraft precisely. Needed to aim a camera or track the Sun.

parts.name: UHF whip antenna
parts.blurb: Two tape-spring whips that pop out after release. Slow, but it works with almost any ground station.

parts.name: S-band patch antenna
parts.blurb: A flat antenna about a hundred times faster than UHF. Needs a dish on the ground.

parts.name: S-band dish antenna
parts.blurb: A small dish that focuses the signal for very high data rates. Heavy, new, and it must be aimed.

parts.name: Microwave radiometer
parts.blurb: Sees through cloud tops to the temperature and rain inside a storm.

parts.name: Multispectral imager
parts.blurb: A camera that photographs land in several colours, including ones our eyes cannot see.

parts.name: Magnetometer on a boom
parts.blurb: Measures Earth's magnetic field. The boom holds it away from the spacecraft's own electronics.

stations.name: University UHF station
stations.blurb: A rooftop antenna run by students. Cheap, UHF only.

stations.name: 3 m S-band dish
stations.blurb: A commercial dish that can receive fast S-band downlinks.

orbits.name: 400 km
orbits.blurb: Close to Earth: sharp images and a strong signal, but air drag brings it down in about a year.

orbits.name: 500 km
orbits.blurb: A common middle choice: a few years in orbit and longer passes over each station.

orbits.name: 600 km
orbits.blurb: Stays up for many years and sees more ground, but the signal is weaker.
